speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I need to ask you some questions to understand what is causing your fever and altered mental state. Can you tell me your age and if you have any history of diabetes or immune system problems?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation, reporting fever without chills and rigors. He denies sore throat, abdominal pain, headache, loose stool, burning micturition, or seizures. Has a history of tics and is currently taking haloperidol.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you. Given your history of tics and current use of haloperidol, I need to assess for signs of Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome. Do you have any muscle rigidity, excessive sweating, or tremors? Also, have you recently started or increased the dose of haloperidol?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Fever and altered mentation. I also have Profuse sweating, Generalized rigidity, Confusion and disorientation, Ability to move all limbs, Normal deep tendon reflexes with bilateral downgoing plantar responses.

speaker: Doctor
text: Those symptoms strongly suggest Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome, but I need to confirm your temperature and check for autonomic instability. REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count, Creatine_Kinase, Electrolytes, Temperature.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: White Blood Cell Count: 14,700/mm3 (elevated); Creatine Kinase: 5600 U/L (elevated); Electrolytes: Data not provided; Temperature: 39.6°C (103.2°F)

speaker: Doctor
text:
The elevated white blood cell count, significantly high creatine kinase, and high fever in the context of haloperidol use and rigidity strongly confirm Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome. I have enough information to proceed.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome
